title: POC Kickoff: Hosting Decision Criteria - Lindberg Energy
summary: Kickoff for a 6-week POC to choose between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment modes. Focus on success criteria (latency, cost, reliability), workload sizing for their document ingestion and chat assistant use case, benchmarking plan (p50/p95, throughput, cold start), timelines, and security/compliance constraints (data residency, KMS, audit logs). Agreed to run two benchmark sweeps (hosted vs dedicated on similar model), produce cost/latency decision matrix, and follow up with a private deployment feasibility assessment if required.
next_steps: Redwood: send POC plan + pricing and benchmark template (Sofia) - due 2026-07-13
Customer: share sample workload traces and SLO targets (Priya) - due 2026-07-10
Schedule technical deep-dive for private deployment feasibility if needed (Marco + Aisha) - by 2026-07-16
action_items: Sofia Chen: Draft POC plan, include cost-per-token and reserved capacity scenarios (due 2026-07-13)
Priya Nair: Export 3 days of traffic traces and worst-case peak minute stats (due 2026-07-10)
Marco Ruiz: Prepare benchmark harness and initial perf script for p50/p95/throughput (due 2026-07-15)
Aisha Gomez: Provide VPC/network constraints and any IP allowlist requirements (due 2026-07-12)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-08 15:00 UTC | Duration 52m
Attendees: Sofia Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Lindberg Head of ML), Jason Lindberg (CTO), Aisha Gomez (Cloud Infra), Tom Hart (Security)

Summary note (auto): kickoff POC to decide hosting mode. Quick agenda run.

[00:00:12] Sofia Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Sofia from Redwood, i'll run the agenda quick. we put together a recommended 6-week POC to compare hosted, dedicated reserved capacity and then a private vpc/on-prem feasibility check.
[00:00:32] Priya Nair: thanks Sofia, excited — we want to validate latency, cost and of course security. big use case is document Q&A + internal chat assistant, about 120k docs initially, indexing + retrieval.
[00:00:48] Jason Lindberg: hi, quick intro from our side, main driver is customer data residency in EU and cost predictability. we also have a hard requirement for 99.9% availability SLA for the chat path.
[00:01:05] Marco Ruiz: hey team, Marco here — for the POC we'll focus on three measurable success criteria: p50/p95 token latency for 512-token prompts, end-to-end request time for retrieval-augmented generation, and cost per 1M tokens. we'll also capture cold-start behavior and throughput (rps / tokens per second).
[00:01:28] Aisha Gomez: quick note on infra — we are cloud-native on GCP, strict VPC peering rules, can't accept public endpoints without a proxy. so hosted would need an edge-proxy, dedicated must support private link, private means we run a package on our VPC or on prem.
[00:01:50] Tom Hart: security checklist: SOC 2, support for customer-managed KMS, audit logs retention 1 year, SSO SAML + RBAC. also need proof of no data exfil for hosted plans.
[00:02:10] Sofia Chen: noted. we'll attach our security whitepaper and SOC2 report. for KMS Redwood supports bring-your-own key for Dedicated/Private and hosted with managed KMS but we can discuss HSM options.
[00:02:30] Priya Nair: can you explain what the dedicated option gives us over hosted? we care about latency more than absolute lowest cost.
[00:02:42] Marco Ruiz: dedicated buys you reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput and isolation — less noisy neighbor variability, lower p95 spikes under load. hosted is faster to start and cheaper at low volume but could have higher variability; private is for when data residency and network controls rule.
[00:03:05] Jason Lindberg: are the models identical across modes? like if we pick a quantized 8-bit variant for cost, is the semantic quality same?
[00:03:16] Marco Ruiz: good question — same model family yes, but quantization can change output distribution slightly. part of the POC is a quality regression test: we run the same evaluation prompts across the variants and flag any regression above our threshold (we usually set 2% delta on key metrics like exact match / BLEU-ish metrics for retrieval flows).
[00:03:40] Sofia Chen: timeline propose: week 0 kickoff (this call), week 1 data handoff + baseline hosted run, week 2 dedicated baseline (reserved sim), week 3-4 tuning (batching, KV cache, sequence lengths), week 5 benchmark sweep and quality eval, week 6 decision review and recommendation.
[00:04:05] Priya Nair: sounds good. for workload sizing we have an average of 18 qps with peak 110 qps for a short burst, avg tokens per request ~240, retrieval step adds ~80ms on our vector DB.
[00:04:26] Marco Ruiz: ok that helps — we'll size dedicated nodes to meet sustained 18 qps with headroom for 2x for spikes, and capture burst performance in hosted mode too.
[00:04:42] Sofia Chen: what are your cost guardrails? annual spend ceiling?
[00:04:47] Jason Lindberg: we want to keep steady-state inference cost under $12k / month initially, but we can flex if dedicated reduces latency significantly.
[00:04:58] Marco Ruiz: noted. we'll produce cost models for hosted (pay-as-you-go), dedicated (reserved monthly) and private (one-time infra + license + ops) with per-token and per-concurrency breakdowns.
[00:05:15] Aisha Gomez: network constraints again — if hosted requires an outbound connection that's fine through an egress proxy, but we need to validate IP allowlist and company firewall rules.
[00:05:30] Tom Hart: also need to confirm retention in hosted mode - we can't store raw documents on Redwood side; embeddings can be ephemeral. is that possible?
[00:05:40] Sofia Chen: yes we have an option to not persist customer payloads; for hosted we propose not retaining raw docs and we can enable ephemeral KV cache plus customer-controlled embeddings lifecycle. we'll document it.
[00:05:58] Priya Nair: benchmarks — what does Redwood measure by default?
[00:06:05] Marco Ruiz: we capture p50/p95/p99, token throughput, GPU utilization, and request-level traces for cold vs warm. our Optimize tool will recommend batching and quantization profiles based on your token-length distribution.
[00:06:22] Jason Lindberg: can you demo the benchmark harness?
[00:06:25] Marco Ruiz: not today in detail — we'll send the harness and initial scripts. plan is: you drop a trace file (we'll provide format), we run hosted baseline, then replay on dedicated config, and we return a spreadsheet with latency/cost rows.
[00:06:40] Sofia Chen: on quality checks — Priya you mentioned evaluation prompts. could you provide a small set of golden prompts and expected outputs?
[00:06:50] Priya Nair: yes we'll provide ~200 eval prompts drawn from internal tickets and transcripts, plus a few adversarial cases.
[00:06:59] Marco Ruiz: perfect — we'll run the eval across model variants and surface any regression where the model drops accuracy or hallucination increases.
[00:07:12] [crosstalk] Aisha Gomez: question about private — if we go private, is there an on-prem package?
[00:07:17] Sofia Chen: yes we have a private deployment option — customer-managed control plane with an on-prem package. typical tradeoffs: more ops work, higher up-front cost, but meets residency and network controls. we usually do a private feasibility deep-dive in parallel if the POC shows reservation is required.
[00:07:35] Tom Hart: does private support our HSM for keys?
[00:07:38] Marco Ruiz: yes, the private stack integrates with customer KMS/HSM and we can map keys via KMIP or cloud KMS connectors.
[00:07:46] Sofia Chen: any hard blockers to start the POC?
[00:07:50] Priya Nair: none, just need a clear plan for the trace export and a point-of-contact for infra work (Aisha).
[00:07:57] Aisha Gomez: I'll be the infra POC. I'll need the exact IPs and ports Redwood will use for hosted baseline, and the dedicated reserved capacity config for network peering.
[00:08:12] Marco Ruiz: we'll provide an architecture note and a minimal network diagram. expect that in the POC plan.
[00:08:20] Sofia Chen: on success criteria let's be explicit: 1) p95 latency < 850ms for 512 tokens on retrieval-augmented path, 2) cost < $12k/mo steady state for chosen path, 3) no critical security gaps (SOC2 + KMS) and 4) quality delta < 2% on evaluation prompts. agree?
[00:08:43] Priya Nair: yes that matches our internal targets, we can negotiate the latency bar if needed.
[00:08:50] Jason Lindberg: what about SLOs and SLA for hosted vs dedicated?
[00:08:53] Sofia Chen: hosted has standard uptime SLA (we'll share exact numbers) and dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets as part of reserved contracts. private SLA is negotiated per enterprise contract.
[00:09:10] Marco Ruiz: technical note — for dedicated we recommend using continuous batching and KV cache pinned to nodes to reduce repeated token compute; we'll test different cache hit ratios during the POC.
[00:09:24] Priya Nair: question — will you run the dedicated baseline on equivalent hardware to what we'd get in production?
[00:09:30] Marco Ruiz: we'll provision similar GPU family and memory config; if you have constraints on specific instance types we can match those. for hosted we will run on our standard fleet and annotate hardware in the results.
[00:09:44] Aisha Gomez: network egress costs — if hosted requires egress from EU to Redwood region, who's responsible?
[00:09:52] Sofia Chen: typically egress is customer-managed; we'll call out bandwidth and bytes in the cost model so you can estimate. Dedicated/private may reduce egress if co-located.
[00:10:05] [00:10:05 - 00:22:00] (detailed technical discussion, benchmarking knobs and approximate calculations)
[00:10:12] Marco Ruiz: quick calc — with your avg 18 qps and 240 tokens per request, that's ~4.3M tokens/day; steady-state monthly ~130M tokens. at hosted rates that maps to X dollars in our sheet, dedicated reserved reduces per-token by ~30% depending on utilization.
[00:12:45] Priya Nair: we also have heavy long-context retrievals occasionally up to 2k tokens — will that skew latency?
[00:12:52] Marco Ruiz: yes longer contexts change kernel paths and memory pressure; we'll include mixed sequence-length runs in the benchmark so you see p95 impact.
[00:14:30] Jason Lindberg: any privacy-preserving options like on-the-fly embedding hashing?
[00:14:35] Sofia Chen: we support no-persist mode and you can configure embeddings to be ephemeral; for additional privacy we can run a transform step in your VPC before outbound.
[00:17:10] [noise / brief hold music — transcription fuzzy]
[00:18:05] Marco Ruiz: we'll prepare two benchmark sweeps: 1) hosted baseline with your trace, 2) dedicated reserved capacity sim. If private is considered we do a quick feasibility checklist and estimate ops effort.
[00:18:30] Aisha Gomez: good. also list needed firewall rules and expected ip ranges.
[00:18:36] Sofia Chen: will do, we'll add that to the POC doc.
[00:19:05] Priya Nair: can you include a comparison matrix for decision criteria? like a table showing latency, cost, security fit, ops overhead for each mode.
[00:19:12] Sofia Chen: yes we'll include a decision matrix with weighted criteria. we can also run a sensitivity analysis on throughput vs cost.
[00:20:01] Jason Lindberg: what's the expected cadence for weekly check-ins?
[00:20:05] Sofia Chen: weekly sync every Friday for 30 minutes; milestone check at week 3 for tuning.
[00:20:12] Priya Nair: ok that works.
[00:20:30] [00:20:30 - 00:34:00] (discussion of eval corpus, golden labels, and regression thresholds)
[00:21:05] Marco Ruiz: regarding evals — we'll compute exact-match, F1 and a hallucination score from human review on a sample. we'll flag any regression > 2% and recommend rollback to a different quant profile.
[00:22:50] Aisha Gomez: if the POC shows hosted meets latency but fails data residency, we may pivot to dedicated with private link or to private entirely. what's the expected lead time for Dedicated reserved capacity?
[00:23:00] Sofia Chen: reserved capacity provisioning is usually 2-3 weeks once contract is signed; we can sometimes accelerate for POC. private on-prem typically 6-10 weeks depending on ops readiness.
[00:23:20] Tom Hart: for procurement, we need a simple one-pager of contract terms and data responsibilities to share with legal.
[00:23:28] Sofia Chen: I'll include a procurement appendix and sample contract language.
[00:23:45] Priya Nair: last question — can Redwood provide a fallback policy if a model variant underperforms in production?
[00:23:52] Marco Ruiz: yes, we support smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants or region-based fallback. we'll show examples in the final report.
[00:24:10] Jason Lindberg: great.
[00:24:15] Sofia Chen: ok recap. action items: Sofia sends POC plan + pricing + network doc; Priya shares traces and eval prompts; Marco prepares benchmark harness and initial run on hosted. weekly Fridays 30m.
[00:24:40] Priya Nair: thanks everyone. excited to get started.
[00:24:45] [end of recorded transcript — remainder of meeting notes and chat links appended]
